slot.brief: Find the equation of a line through a given point making a specified angle/slope relation with a given line.

stem: The line $y=\dfrac{x}{\sqrt3}+1$ has inclination $\theta$. Find the equation of the line through $(1,-2)$ whose inclination is $2\theta$.

verdicts.working: The given line has slope \(1/\sqrt3\), so \(\theta=\pi/6\). Thus \(2\theta=\pi/3\), with slope \(\sqrt3\). Through \((1,-2)\): \(y+2=\sqrt3(x-1)\), which is option A.

working:
Given line slope $=\tan 30^\circ=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$, so $\theta=30^\circ$.\nRequired slope $=\tan(2\theta)=\tan 60^\circ=\sqrt3$.\n$y+2=\sqrt3(x-1)\Rightarrow \sqrt3x-y-\sqrt3-2=0$.

Independent check: The given line has slope \(1/\sqrt3\), so \(\theta=\pi/6\). Thus \(2\theta=\pi/3\), with slope \(\sqrt3\). Through \((1,-2)\): \(y+2=\sqrt3(x-1)\), which is option A.
